chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn al-Khalid al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bakir, from Zurarah who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Islam is founded upon ten pillars: bearing witness that there is no god but God, which is the creed; prayer, which is the obligation; fasting, which is paradise; alms-tax, which is purification; pilgrimage, which is the law; striving, which is campaigning; enjoining good, which is fidelity; forbidding evil, which is the proof; community, which is harmony; and infallibility, which is obedience.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten pillars of Islam according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this unique enumeration of ten pillars in *Al-Khisal*, distinguishing it from the more common five or seven by including *Al-Amr bi-l-Ma'ruf* (commanding good) and *Al-Nahy 'an al-Munkar* (forbidding evil) as foundational structural elements rather than mere obligations. This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, reflects the Shia emphasis on *Al-Amr bi-l-Ma'ruf* as a core pillar of community cohesion and divine proof (*Al-Hujjah*), linking the concept of *Al-Jama'ah* (congregation) directly to social unity (*Al-Alafah*).
